pitch.title: The Harvest Calendar Veto
pitch.ordinaryGood: The Thalassic Houses still coordinate storm refuge, planting calendars, and food rescue across shoals that the Benefactor harvest model cannot reach in time.
pitch.pressure: Planetary integration would make the shared harvest calendar mandatory before the migrating reefs and outer shoals can be represented in it.
pitch.affectedActor: Reef listeners, outer-shoal growers, and households whose seasons do not fit the integrated model
pitch.evidenceLimit: Deep-tide testimony demonstrates strategic refusal, but it cannot establish one unified ocean speaker or one calendar for every migration.
pitch.concreteCost: Delaying certification risks spoiled stores and renewed scarcity, while certifying now gives dynasties and patrons a single schedule capable of erasing every unmodeled season.
pitch.persistentChange: The harvest calendar must accept locally governed forks, publish dependency and failure modes, and give reef listeners standing over revisions that affect migration.
pitch.controlQuestion: Who may certify one harvest calendar when delay can starve people and speed can erase the seasons of actors the model cannot represent?

pitch.title: The Reef Translation License
pitch.ordinaryGood: Coastal councils need a repeatable way to distinguish ordinary reef migration from strategic refusal before rerouting medicine, fishing, and rescue traffic.
pitch.pressure: The first successful translation is being treated as a universal administrative interface to the entire ocean.
pitch.affectedActor: Physicians, navigators, and reef communities who will bear decisions made through a translation none of them fully control
pitch.evidenceLimit: The translated patterns establish strategic refusal in one intervention, but the instruments alter the habitat and cannot establish a single speaker, stable vocabulary, or permanent consent.
pitch.concreteCost: Refusing a license leaves rescue traffic blind, while granting one turns a contaminated translation into compulsory planetary testimony.
pitch.persistentChange: Every translation must carry provenance, competing renderings, expiration conditions, and a right for represented ecologies to refuse administrative reuse.
pitch.controlQuestion: When a translation is useful enough to save lives but too contaminated to speak for a world, who may license what it is allowed to decide?

pitch.title: The Dead-Star Customs Court
pitch.ordinaryGood: Publishing the route lets independent witnesses verify the dead-star archive and prevents either patrons or dynasties from burying it again.
pitch.pressure: The public route is attracting salvagers, pilgrims, patrons, and frightened city fleets before Ilyon has law for what may cross in either direction.
pitch.affectedActor: Clinic networks and coastal populations whose survival could be disrupted by a route opened in the name of evidentiary freedom
pitch.evidenceLimit: The ruined geometry establishes lineage and sequence, but damaged records leave motive contested and cannot classify every object or visitor now approaching the route.
pitch.concreteCost: Closing the route protects fragile systems by recreating private custody, while leaving it ungoverned lets every threatened power turn verification into extraction or quarantine.
pitch.persistentChange: The route receives a public customs court with evidentiary custody, contamination receipts, refusal rights, and no single faction able to close or monopolize passage.
pitch.controlQuestion: Who governs an evidentiary route after making it public creates the very constituencies capable of capturing or closing it?

pitch.title: The Night Market Quiet Permit
pitch.ordinaryGood: The night market carries food variety, repairs, courtship, performance, and trust between layers that otherwise meet only through emergency offices.
pitch.pressure: Quiet Hours proposes to keep the market open only as a rotating technical permit whose wake allocation can be revoked without a public hearing.
pitch.affectedActor: Surface households, growers, cooks, and children whose ordinary life remains classified as discretionary signature
pitch.evidenceLimit: The thermal audit can trace present heat and traffic, but the measurement changes the flow and cannot establish the future capacity of damaged sinks.
pitch.concreteCost: A guaranteed market schedule increases predictable wake, while a revocable permit preserves food and public life only at the pleasure of the emergency office.
pitch.persistentChange: The market receives a bounded public signature budget, review dates, named denial costs, and standing for the surface households carrying its shifted wake.
pitch.controlQuestion: Who may reduce public life to a revocable technical permit when the same office defines both the danger and the evidence allowed to contest it?

pitch.title: The Relay Contamination Hearing
pitch.ordinaryGood: A witnessed relay test could distinguish a living threat from inherited emergency doctrine before the district sacrifices another generation to Hush.
pitch.pressure: The response fragment is being used both to justify permanent concealment and to demand immediate public recognition of the surface households.
pitch.affectedActor: Residents governed by the Alarm and surface families whose recognition may itself become a locating signal
pitch.evidenceLimit: The fragment proves activity and inherited target logic, but it does not establish the lattice's reach, present intent, or ability to locate the district.
pitch.concreteCost: A stronger test may complete the target handshake, while refusing every test makes emergency authority impossible to falsify.
pitch.persistentChange: Future contact requires isolated challenges, independent witnesses, explicit stop conditions, and an audit ledger separating what was observed from what remains feared.
pitch.controlQuestion: How may a district test the danger that legitimizes permanent emergency rule when the conclusive test may also deliver the district to that danger?

pitch.title: The Sleeping Market Inheritance Court
pitch.ordinaryGood: Recognizing the sleeping market restores erased residents, machine continuities, and household records to the district census.
pitch.pressure: Recognition creates claims on housing, heat, archives, and routes already allocated by generations who believed the market was residue.
pitch.affectedActor: Present households and the newly recognized continuities whose legitimate claims cannot all be satisfied by the same rooms and records
pitch.evidenceLimit: Recovered ledgers establish continuing families and omitted deaths, but they do not prove that every preserved continuity has the same legal identity or present preference.
pitch.concreteCost: Immediate restitution can dispossess living households, while delay repeats the erasure by treating recognized claimants as evidence rather than residents.
pitch.persistentChange: The census gains an inheritance court that records competing continuity claims, temporary habitat rights, archive custody, and decisions that remain revisable when better evidence appears.
pitch.controlQuestion: Who inherits a district after recognition returns people and continuities to a map whose homes, records, and resources were already reassigned?
